benchmarks.name: MMAE
benchmarks.description: Tests instruction following and preservation across speech, music, sound, and their mixtures with 2,000 cases (≈8.0 h), six complexity levels, and 17,741 verification rubrics.
benchmarks.evaluation: MLLM — Qwen3-Omni judges individual rubrics with majority voting, yielding Instruction Following Rate (IFR), Consistency Rate (CR), and Exact Match Rate (EMR).

results.label: Single model
results.text: On the full benchmark in the original comparison, Step-Audio-EditX leads IFR (44.86%) and CR (58.88%), while Ming-UniAudio leads EMR (3.20%); Audio-Omni reaches 4.99% EMR on the separate 801-case, ≤10 s subset. The newer AuK baseline without Prompt Enhancer reports 7.58% EMR on the 1,003-case single-operation subset.

results.label: Agent / LLM-assisted system
results.text: The challenge agent baseline, combining an LLM router with DSP, SAM-Audio, and AuK, reports 7.45% EMR, 44.06% IFR, and 74.63% CR on all 2,000 cases. Separately, AuK-Flash with Prompt Enhancer reaches 13.85% EMR on MMAE-Speech only; these scopes are not directly comparable.

benchmarks.name: SpeechEditBench
benchmarks.description: Separates edit success from linguistic-content preservation in bilingual speech editing through 4,700 cases (≈9.4 h) covering seven atomic attributes and multi-attribute instructions.
benchmarks.evaluation: Hybrid — ASR, speaker verification, acoustic/prosodic measurements, and a Gemini audio judge produce target success, content-preservation success, and joint success.

results.label: Single model
results.text: By task, GPT-Realtime reaches 96.67% content, 68.67% style, and 47.00% paralinguistic joint success; Gemini-Live reaches 27.79% emotion and 11.00% compositional joint success. The newer AuK comparison reports 71.33% prosody joint success, but covers only five task types.

benchmarks.name: Ming-Freeform-Audio-Edit
benchmarks.description: Evaluates timestamp-free, instruction-guided speech changes with ≈3.3k instruction cases across Basic/Full lexical edits and five attribute-control tasks in Chinese and English.
benchmarks.evaluation: Hybrid — Whisper/Paraformer and WavLM measure transcription and speaker preservation; signal measurements assess speed/volume control, and an audio-capable judge assesses emotion/dialect conversion.

results.label: Single model
results.text: AuK reports 3.09% / 3.96% WER and 91.47% / 85.25% edit accuracy on Full Chinese / English, averaged over deletion, insertion, and substitution; these lead the checked lexical-editing comparisons.

benchmarks.name: Step-Audio-Edit-Benchmark
benchmarks.description: Evaluates expressive and iterative speech editing using 8 speakers and 8,800 text prompts for emotion, speaking style, and paralinguistics, with reference voices released and output duration dependent on synthesis.
benchmarks.evaluation: MLLM — Gemini-2.5-Pro measures emotion/style classification accuracy and rates paralinguistic realization on a 1–3 scale.

results.label: Single model
results.text: Step-Audio-EditX reports 71.0% emotion accuracy and 66.2% style accuracy after three editing iterations, and 2.89/3 paralinguistic score after one iteration in the published native-input comparison.

benchmarks.name: LyricEditBench
benchmarks.description: Tests melody-preserving lyric modification with 7,200 bilingual cases, each using a ≤15 s melody reference, across six lyric-editing scenarios and both self-timbre and cross-timbre settings.
benchmarks.editing: Semantic; Instance; Composite (lyric changes together with singer-identity transfer in the cross-timbre setting).
benchmarks.evaluation: Expert models — singing ASR for Phoneme Error Rate (PER), WavLM for speaker similarity, RMVPE for F0 correlation, and VocalVerse2 for vocal quality, supplemented by human listening tests.

results.label: Single model
results.text: YingMusic-Singer outperforms Vevo2 on lyric intelligibility, melody adherence, and vocal quality in the published comparison; for Chinese partial substitution, self-timbre, it achieves 2.14% PER and 0.9615 F0 correlation. Vevo2 retains an advantage in speaker similarity on this setting.

benchmarks.name: ZoME-Bench
benchmarks.description: Provides 1,100 music-editing cases (10 s each; ≈3.1 h counted per case) across instrument, genre, mood, rhythm, melody, and background changes, with captions and instructions supporting both prompt-based and instruction-based evaluation.
benchmarks.evaluation: Expert models — audio–text alignment and perceptual/structural measures such as CLAP, LPAPS, and chroma similarity, supplemented by human ratings.

results.label: Single model / non-agent editor
results.text: In the later AnchorSteer instrument-editing comparison, its conditioned variant achieves the highest CLAP (0.395) and GAP (0.279) among the compared methods, while its unconditioned variant preserves more structure (chroma similarity 0.470, versus 0.238 for the conditioned variant).

benchmarks.name: MelodiaEdit
benchmarks.description: Evaluates instrument, genre, and mood changes while preserving musical structure through 2,015 editing pairs drawn from 180 released source clips (≈0.86 h unique audio), combining synthesized and real music.
benchmarks.evaluation: Expert models — CLAP, LPAPS, chroma similarity, FAD, and combined adherence/preservation scores, supplemented by human listening tests.

results.label: Single model
results.text: In the published comparison, Melodia has the highest CLAP (0.39) and lowest LPAPS (3.11) on MelodiaEdit; MusicMagus instead leads chroma similarity (0.73) and FAD (0.57), illustrating the alignment–preservation trade-off.

links.label: GitHub
links.note: data release; evaluation implementation not released

benchmarks.name: AvED-Bench
benchmarks.description: Tests synchronized sound-event and visual-entity replacement using 110 audio-video clips (10 s each; ≈18.3 min) curated from VGGSound with source/target descriptions.
benchmarks.editing: Instance; editing the video alongside the sound does not by itself constitute Composite audio editing.
benchmarks.evaluation: Expert models — embedding-based audio–text/audio–video alignment and perceptual preservation metrics, supplemented by human judgments.

results.label: Single model / non-agent system
results.text: The later CoherentAVEdit comparison reports the strongest listening-test results for VACE → CoherentAVEdit: 3.7/5 audio–text fidelity, 3.8/5 audio–visual alignment, and 3.9/5 structure preservation on a six-video subjective subset; this is a sequential, non-agent pipeline, not a single joint model or a full-set aggregate ranking.

benchmarks.name: AVE-Compass
benchmarks.description: Diagnoses instruction following and preservation in free-form audio-video editing through 145 source videos (up to 10 s), 196 instructions, and 2,688 checklist items covering 28 editing operations.
benchmarks.editing: Acoustic; Semantic; Instance; Composite (when the audio request itself crosses categories).
benchmarks.evaluation: Hybrid — checklist-based MLLM judging combines with expert models for audio quality, audio–video/lip synchronization, and visual preservation.

results.label: Single model
results.text: On the official leaderboard, Wan2.7 leads overall Editing Intent at 42.4/100 (audio: 24.8); LTX2 has the highest audio-only Editing Intent among the listed single models (26.4/100).

results.label: Agent
results.text: AVE-Agent (Wan) leads with 59.8/100 overall Editing Intent and 50.2/100 audio Editing Intent on the same leaderboard.

metrics.name: WER / CER ↓
metrics.description: ASR transcription errors relative to the requested words or characters.
metrics.inputs: Target transcript; ASR transcript of the edited output.

metrics.name: Emotion classification accuracy ↑
metrics.description: Agreement between the predicted emotion and the requested emotion label.
metrics.inputs: Target emotion label; an emotion classifier with a matching label set.

metrics.name: CLAP audio–text similarity ↑
metrics.description: Cosine similarity between output audio and the desired audio description.
metrics.inputs: Caption describing the desired result; a specified CLAP checkpoint.

metrics.name: Event Occurrence Score (EOS) ↑
metrics.description: Minimum event-level CLAP similarity after text-guided source separation; checks coverage of requested events.
metrics.inputs: Desired event descriptions; event decomposition and separated event tracks.

metrics.name: Speaker embedding cosine similarity ↑
metrics.description: Retention of speaker identity in the edited speech.
metrics.inputs: Source speaker audio; the same speaker-verification encoder for both recordings.

metrics.name: Multi-resolution STFT distance ↓
metrics.description: Spectral convergence and log-magnitude differences across several time–frequency resolutions.
metrics.inputs: Aligned source/output audio from the non-edited regions.

metrics.name: CLAP audio–audio similarity ↑
metrics.description: Semantic similarity between source and edited audio embeddings; a broad preservation proxy.
metrics.inputs: Source audio; matching non-target regions or stems for local comparison.

metrics.name: LPAPS distance ↓
metrics.description: Perceptual distance between audio representations from a pretrained feature network.
metrics.inputs: Source audio; aligned non-edited regions for local comparison.

metrics.name: Boundary error ↓
metrics.description: Mean or median absolute timing error of predicted speech-segment boundaries.
metrics.inputs: Manual boundary annotations and predicted boundaries, in the same time unit.

metrics.name: Word-level Dynamic Time Warping (WDTW) ↓
metrics.description: Length-normalized DTW distance over matched word segments in source and edited speech.
metrics.inputs: Source and edited speech; both transcripts and word-level forced alignments.

metrics.name: Melody accuracy ↑
metrics.description: Frame-wise agreement of the dominant pitch class between reference and edited music.
metrics.inputs: Reference melody/audio; aligned pitch-class sequences.

metrics.name: F0 Pearson correlation ↑
metrics.description: Correlation between reference and output vocal-pitch contours.
metrics.inputs: Reference vocal audio; aligned F0 contours extracted with the same model.

metrics.name: Chroma similarity / Chroma DTW similarity ↑
metrics.description: Pitch-class distribution similarity, or frame-wise similarity after DTW alignment.
metrics.inputs: Source/reference music; consistently extracted chromagrams.

metrics.name: Beat F1 ↑
metrics.description: Precision–recall balance of matching beat timestamps within a 70 ms tolerance.
metrics.inputs: Reference and output beat timestamps.

metrics.name: Dynamics correlation ↑
metrics.description: Frame-wise Pearson correlation of reference and output loudness trajectories.
metrics.inputs: Reference dynamics/audio; aligned loudness trajectories.

metrics.name: Structural pairwise F-measure / ARI ↑
metrics.description: Agreement of musical section assignments, with ARI correcting for chance agreement.
metrics.inputs: Source/reference and output segmentations in a shared time frame.

metrics.name: Event Sequence Score (ESS) ↑
metrics.description: Kendall-style rank agreement between the described and detected event order.
metrics.inputs: Desired event ordering; onset estimates from separated event tracks.

metrics.name: MOS / CMOS ↑
metrics.description: Human ratings of output quality or comparative quality against another recording.
metrics.inputs: Listeners and a task-specific rating protocol; comparison audio for CMOS.

metrics.name: MOSNet predicted MOS ↑
metrics.description: Automatic prediction of speech naturalness ratings, developed for voice conversion.
metrics.inputs: Edited speech.

metrics.name: UTMOSv2 predicted MOS ↑
metrics.description: Predicted naturalness MOS, developed for high-quality synthetic speech.
metrics.inputs: Edited speech.

metrics.name: SpeechJudge-GRM (pairwise)
metrics.description: Paired naturalness ratings and preference, accompanied by a generated explanation.
metrics.inputs: Target transcript and two candidate speech recordings for the same text.

metrics.name: DNSMOS P.835 ↑
metrics.description: Predicted speech-signal, background-noise and overall quality scores.
metrics.inputs: Edited speech.

metrics.name: NISQA ↑
metrics.description: Predicted overall speech quality and degradation dimensions; NISQA-TTS targets synthetic-speech naturalness.
metrics.inputs: Edited speech; the appropriate NISQA checkpoint.

metrics.name: PAM ↑
metrics.description: No-reference audio quality from an audio–language model using contrasting positive and negative quality prompts.
metrics.inputs: Edited audio; fixed quality prompts and the PAM implementation's MS-CLAP backbone.

metrics.name: PESQ ↑
metrics.description: Reference-based perceptual speech quality after degradation or restoration.
metrics.inputs: Corresponding clean target speech; 8 kHz narrowband or 16 kHz wideband mode.

metrics.name: STOI ↑
metrics.description: Estimated intelligibility of degraded or enhanced speech.
metrics.inputs: Time-aligned clean target speech.

metrics.name: SI-SDR ↑
metrics.description: Target-signal reconstruction fidelity after compensating for a global scale difference.
metrics.inputs: Time-aligned target waveform or isolated target source.

metrics.name: NOMAD distance ↓
metrics.description: Perceptual speech degradation measured in a learned embedding space.
metrics.inputs: Clean speech references; matching linguistic content is not required.

metrics.name: SpeechBERTScore ↑
metrics.description: Reference-aware speech quality proxy using greedy matching of self-supervised speech features.
metrics.inputs: Natural reference speech; a fixed encoder, layer and precision/recall/F1 variant.

metrics.name: Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD) ↓
metrics.description: Distance between output and reference audio-embedding distributions.
metrics.inputs: Reference audio collection; the same embedding backbone and preprocessing.

metrics.name: AuditEval (SSL / LLM)
metrics.description: Quality, editing relevance and faithfulness to the source.
metrics.inputs: Source and edited audio; original and target descriptions.

metrics.name: MuseCPEval
metrics.description: Harmony, rhythm, structure and melody preservation, with additional timbre metrics in the toolkit.
metrics.inputs: Source and edited music; selected musical attributes to preserve.

metrics.name: MMAE rubric evaluator (Qwen3-Omni)
metrics.description: Instruction Following Rate (IFR), Consistency Rate (CR) and Exact Match Rate (EMR).
metrics.inputs: Source/output audio, editing instructions and sample-specific MMAE rubrics.

metrics.name: Audiobox Aesthetics
metrics.description: Content Enjoyment (CE), Content Usefulness (CU), Production Complexity (PC) and Production Quality (PQ).
metrics.inputs: Edited audio only.

metrics.name: SongEval scoring model
metrics.description: Overall coherence, memorability, vocal breathing/phrasing naturalness, structural clarity and overall musicality.
metrics.inputs: Full-length song audio with vocals and accompaniment.

metrics.name: MuseCritic
metrics.description: Coherence, musicality, memorability, structural clarity and vocal naturalness; returns scores and a natural-language critique.
metrics.inputs: Full-length song audio; the released aesthetic rubric.
